findings.title: prune <-> workspace-sync re-add loop: pruned files resurrect within the hour, retention never converges
findings.evidence: monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/run-2026-04-26T17-05-12Z.json (policy: 7d retention, keep 20) deleted by prune commit b8e3c000 2026-06-06T08:06Z, RE-ADDED by workspace-sync commit 73f18678 at 08:22Z — 16 minutes later. Same file also deleted 0901036d (06-04) and re-added ecd8f909. Dir holds 892 files vs expected ~20-170; oldest is 42 days old. Mechanism: prune deletes in git from its clone, but FUSE cannot unlink, so FUSE copies persist forever; universal-pusher sees file-in-FUSE-absent-in-git and pushes it back. Affects ALL pruned categories (~1,400 files/day delete+re-add churn per daily prune summaries: 1348 on 06-04, 1440 on 06-06), plus duplicate records appended to archive JSONLs every cycle (archives grow unboundedly with dupes).
findings.recommendation: Needs own PROP next run (suggest PROP-082): make workspace-sync's universal-pusher policy-aware — skip pushing files whose filename-embedded timestamp is older than the prune retention window for that category (reuse parseFilenameTimestamp + the policies table), OR have prune write a pruned-manifest deny-list the pusher consults. Operator-side alternative: allow_cowork_file_delete + rm of FUSE copies (proven 2026-05-19) but that is manual and ~5,000 files. Related: DIRECTIVE-20260521-002 (audit-files no-round-trip) is the same defect family.
